issues.t: Intake or head gasket failure and coolant loss
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, overheating, the heater going cold, or white smoke from the exhaust.
issues.why: The gaskets on this older GM V6 commonly start leaking at higher mileage, letting coolant escape outside the engine or seep into it.
issues.next: Check the coolant level often. If the engine runs hot, pull over and shut it off, then have the gaskets pressure-tested before the engine is damaged.

issues.sym: The heat stays cold no matter the setting, or the temperature does not change, and the defroster cannot clear the windshield well.
issues.why: The door that blends hot and cold air, or the plastic shaft and actuator that move it, breaks inside the dash.
issues.next: Have the blend door and actuator checked. Until it is fixed, make sure you can keep the windshield clear in cold or damp weather.

issues.t: AWD driveshaft center bearing or U-joint wear
issues.sym: A vibration that builds around highway speed, a clunk when taking off, or grinding from under the middle of the vehicle.
issues.why: On all-wheel-drive models the support bearing in the middle of the rear driveshaft and the U-joints wear out. A badly worn joint can let the shaft come loose.
issues.next: Have the driveshaft and its bearing inspected soon if you feel new vibration or hear clunks. Do not wait for it to get worse.

issues.sym: The key is hard to turn or will not come out of the ignition, sometimes along with trouble starting.
issues.why: The ignition lock cylinder or switch wears and starts to bind.
issues.next: Do not force the key. Have the lock cylinder and switch checked before it leaves you unable to start or shut off the car.

issues.sym: The oil level is far below full between changes, a low oil pressure warning, blue smoke, or knocking when oil runs low.
issues.why: The piston rings in this engine can clog and let oil past into the cylinders. Running low on oil also wears the timing chain faster. GM offered extended coverage on some of these engines, but those programs have ended.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups and keep it topped up. If the oil light comes on or the engine knocks, stop and add oil before driving on, and have the engine checked.

issues.sym: A check engine light with camshaft timing codes, a rattle at cold start, rough running or reduced power.
issues.why: The timing chains and their guides wear and stretch early on this V6. GM issued a service bulletin with replacement chain kits.
issues.next: Do not ignore timing codes or a cold-start rattle. A badly stretched chain can jump and wreck the engine, so get it repaired promptly.

issues.sym: One or both wipers stop moving, sometimes with a clunk at the base of the windshield.
issues.why: A ball socket in the wiper linkage corrodes, wears and pops apart. GM recalled some years and gave extended coverage on others.
issues.next: Losing wipers in rain or snow is dangerous. Have the dealer check your VIN for the wiper recall or special coverage and replace the wiper linkage.

issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive with the engine still running, or a clunk or vibration from the right front.
issues.why: The short shaft that carries power to the right front wheel can crack and separate. If it fails, the vehicle can also roll when parked without the parking brake. A recall covered this.
issues.next: Check for the open recall by VIN. Always set the parking brake, and if drive is lost, stop and have the vehicle towed.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak from missing endcap bolts
issues.sym: Fluid leaking under the front of the vehicle, slipping, delayed engagement, or loss of drive.
issues.why: Bolts may be missing from an endcap on the transmission part that supports the engine start-stop system. Fluid can leak onto hot exhaust parts. A recall covered this.
issues.next: Check for the open recall. If you see fluid leaking or the transmission slips, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Power loss or misfire in very cold weather
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power, shaking or misfires, and a check engine light, usually on frigid winter days.
issues.why: Moisture from the engine's crankcase ventilation can freeze inside the turbo's charge-air cooler. Dealers have replaced the cooler and related grille parts.
issues.next: Have a dealer read the codes and check the charge-air cooler. Avoid heavy acceleration until it is looked at.

issues.t: Fuel tank seam leak on AWD models
issues.sym: A gasoline smell near the back of the vehicle or wet stains near the tank or filler.
issues.why: A seam on the fuel tank in some AWD models may not be sealed properly. A recall covered this.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside away from buildings and do not drive until the recall work is done.

issues.sym: The vehicle feels like it is held back, a hot or burning smell from a rear wheel, or uneven braking.
issues.why: The wrong lubricant used in some rear calipers can make the seals swell so the brakes do not release fully. A recall covered this.
issues.next: Check for the open recall. If a wheel smells hot or the brakes drag, stop driving and have them inspected.

issues.t: Engine stall from weak fuel pump module
issues.sym: Stalling or hesitation while driving, hard starting, or a check engine light for a lean condition.
issues.why: The fuel pump module may not supply enough fuel consistently. A recall covered this.
issues.next: Check for the open recall by VIN. If the engine stalls or hesitates, get it repaired before driving in traffic.

issues.t: Door striker can break and door may open
issues.sym: A door that does not latch firmly, pops open, or a door-ajar warning while driving.
issues.why: The striker that the door latches onto can fracture. A recall covered this.
issues.next: Check for the open recall right away. If a door will not stay latched, do not carry passengers in that seat until it is fixed.

issues.t: Coolant leak at the water pump
issues.sym: The coolant level drops, a low coolant warning, a sweet smell, or pink or orange crust near the water pump.
issues.why: Coolant can seep from the water pump or its housing. GM issued a preliminary bulletin to help dealers find the leak point.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant level and have the leak repaired under warranty. Stop driving if the engine overheats.
